records.name: Hong Kong
records.summary_text: A special administrative region running its own legal system under a constitutional settlement: trans claims here have been fought in court more than legislated. Same-sex conduct is not criminalised, and the apex court in 2023 ruled full sex-reassignment surgery must not be a precondition for changing the gender marker on the compulsory identity card — reversing a 2019 high-court loss in the same litigation. records.name: Western Sahara
records.summary_text:
A disputed North African territory under military administration by a neighbouring state, whose penal code governs any visitor: same-sex intimacy is criminalised (six months to three years) with wide police discretion, and morality articles are the tool turned on visibly trans people — rights reviews document involuntary outing, expression discrepancies at checkpoints and registries, no gender-affirming healthcare, and no legal gender recognition (a 2021 path covers intersex people only); the administering state's religious establishment has condemned transition.
